key_insight: Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU) selectively resists recovery of deleted knowledge while preserving the ability to learn new tasks by matching the reference model to the same simulated update.
engineering_relevance: For LLM-based engineering tools, UMU could help preserve privacy and safety safeguards during later fine-tuning; this study does not evaluate solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling tasks.
method: Initialize defended and undefended reference models from the same unlearned model.
Apply the same simulated relearning update to both, using the updated reference to guide preservation.
Use new-task learning performance to guide model selection.
evidence_signal: Across TOFU and FaithUn evaluations with Llama and Qwen and three base unlearning methods, UMU reduced harmful and benign relearning by an average of 30.4 and 9.9 points, respectively, while increasing new-task accuracy by 3.5 points.
watch_item: Robustness to real-world fine-tuning updates beyond the simulated relearning conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
